direct_answer: Thumb base osteoarthritis can make opening jars, turning keys and writing painful. Gadgets with bigger handles, splints, hand exercises and pain relief can help. Ask your GP about hand therapy if daily tasks are getting harder.
author: Louis Maxwell
reviewer_credentials: First Contact Practitioner, HCPC PH128483, CSP member

content:
Thumb pain can affect many daily tasks.

This guide covers practical help. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Grip gadgets

  • Jar openers.
  • Key turners.
  • Thick-handled cutlery and pens.

Splints

A thumb splint may ease pain.

Exercises

A hand therapist can show suitable exercises.

Pain relief

Topical anti-inflammatories may help; check with a pharmacist.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is surgery an option?

Sometimes, for severe symptoms.

Will it get worse?

It varies.
